```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse  = TRUE,
  comment   = "#>",
  fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4
)
library(kagu)
set.seed(42)
```

## Define the causal structure

A Kagu model is a DAG — a named list mapping each node to its parent nodes.

```{r dag}
dag <- list(
  education = c(),
  experience = c(),
  income = c("education", "experience")
)

model <- KaguModel$new(dag = dag)
model$plot_dag()
```

## Simulate data and fit

```{r data}
N          <- 500
education  <- rnorm(N, 14, 2)
experience <- rnorm(N, 10, 5)
income     <- 3000 + 500 * education + 200 * experience + rnorm(N, sd = 2000)

data <- data.frame(
  education  = education,
  experience = experience,
  income     = income
)
```

```{r fit, results = "hide"}
model$fit(data, draws = 1000, tune = 1000, chains = 4)
```

## Causal effects

```{r unit-effect}
# Unit effect at the mean — equivalent to a regression coefficient
effect <- model$effects("education", "income")
effect$summary()
```

```{r sd-effect}
# Effect of a 1-SD increase in education
effect_sd <- model$effects("education", "income", std_units = TRUE)
effect_sd$summary()
```

```{r contrast}
# Explicit contrast: 12 years vs 16 years of education
effect_contrast <- model$effects("education", "income", values = c(12, 16))
effect_contrast$summary()
```

```{r plot-effect}
effect$plot()
```

## Dose-response curve

```{r sweep}
sweep <- model$effects("education", "income", sweep = TRUE)
sweep$plot()
```

## Model summary

```{r summary}
model$summary()
```

## Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics}
model$diagnostics("income")
```

## Save and load

```{r save-load}
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
model$save(tmp)
loaded <- KaguModel$load(tmp)
loaded$effects("education", "income")$summary()
```
